reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports spray-coating of 2D HEA nanoflakes and their tribocatalytic, friction-reducing behavior at room temperature under high load, but it does not address high-temperature stability, film formation on CoCrFeNi, or performance up to 800 °C. E2 highlights solvent-dependent performance and failure in water, which is not directly relevant to the proposed dry sliding mechanism. Thus, only the room-temperature coating and catalytic premises are partially supported, while the high-temperature and matrix-specific claims lack evidence.
premises: 2D HEA nanoflakes can be spray-coated onto a substrate
The nanoflake coating exhibits tribocatalytic activity under sliding in ambient conditions
Tribocatalysis produces a lubricious amorphous film that reduces friction and wear
The tribofilm remains intact and effective from room temperature to 800 °C
The mechanism is effective on a CoCrFeNi matrix
